item.title: Deportees Turn to TikTok to Document Life Starting Over
item.description: On TikTok, men and women sent back after living in the United States are documenting the reality of starting over — and finding an audience.

item.title: ‘This Hour Has 22 Minutes,’ a Canadian Sketch Show, Beats American Late Night to the Punchline
item.description: The long-running comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes” is having a heyday playing with the fraught relationship between President Trump and Canada.
item.dc:creator: Shawna Richer
item.media:credit: Carolina Andrade for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Critch, a veteran cast member of “This Hour Has 22 Minutes,” plays President Trump on the show.

item.title: 75 Years On, the National Ballet of Canada ‘Remains the Icon’
item.description: The dance company started on a shoestring and went on to become internationally acclaimed.

item.title: Carney Commits Canada to Becoming European Union’s First ‘Associate Member’
item.description: The move is part of the Canadian prime minister’s effort to reduce American influence over Canada and expand trade to other parts of the world.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday during the 21st E.U.-Canada summit in Montreal, Quebec.

item.title: Could El Salvador’s Bukele Be Haiti’s Savior?
item.description: The Salvadoran government dispatched more than 2,000 troops to Haiti this week in an extraordinary deployment on foreign soil.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles
item.media:credit: Michael Anthony Adams/The New York Times
item.media:description: A Salvadoran gunner in a UH-1N Twin Huey helicopter during an aerial patrol over Port-au-Prince last month. Some Salvadoran troops are members of a U.N.-backed international force in Haiti.

item.title: Colombia’s ‘Narcoterrorist’ Crackdown Raises Questions Over Killings
item.description: Military-involved deaths have roiled a country with an iron-fisted new president — and a history of extrajudicial killings.
item.dc:creator: Simón Posada, Annie Correal and Federico Rios
item.media:credit: Federico Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: Yuli Motta at her home in Guaviare province, Colombia. She says she witnessed the fatal shooting of Luis Carlos Mojica by members of the Colombian military last month.

item.title: Venezuelan Opposition Leader Thanks Trump But Marks Distance from Washington
item.description: Finally home in Caracas, María Corina Machado called for elections next year, and said her return was organized by her team, not any government.
item.dc:creator: Julie Turkewitz and Isayen Herrera
item.media:description: Maria Corina Machado in Caracas, Venezuela, on Thursday.

item.title: Cuba’s Foreign Minister: We’ll Outlast Trump
item.description: The Trump administration is carrying out the most intense pressure campaign on Cuba in decades. The Cuban government says its plan is simply to endure.
item.dc:creator: Jack Nicas
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla of Cuba during an interview with The New York Times this week.

item.title: Why Miami Is a Destination for Latin America’s Political Exiles
item.description: The city’s Hispanic majority, news media reach and air links to Latin America have made it an ideal base for politicians escaping their home countries.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado and Victor Mather
item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro arriving at Opa Locka Executive Airport in Miami on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.
item.description: President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a presidential election in Brazil and faces multiple criminal investigations there, could enter the United States, U.S. officials said.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong, Ana Ionova, Hamed Aleaziz and Tyler Pager
item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro after arriving at Opa Locka airport near Miami on Wednesday.

item.title: Haiti Postpones Elections as Gang Violence Runs Rampant
item.description: Haiti is in the throes of debilitating gang violence, which has kept officials from organizing an election to pick a new president.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles
item.media:credit: Adriana Zehbrauskas for The New York Times
item.media:description: A mural depicting Haiti’s last elected president, Jovenel Moïse, who was elected in 2016, and assassinated in 2021.

item.title: After 28 Years Walking the Globe, Karl Bushby Is Almost Home
item.description: Karl Bushby has walked 31,000 miles, crossing some of the world’s harshest landscapes. He plans to reach his mother’s house in England next week.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:credit: Sam Bush for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mr. Bushby in London. He said his journey was a reminder of people’s kindness.

item.title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Who Helped End One-Party Rule in Mexico, Dies at 92
item.description: Mr. Cárdenas, the only son of a Mexican president, never won the office but became a leading figure in the country’s democratic transformation.
item.dc:creator: Anthony DePalma
item.media:credit: Luis Barron/Eyepix, via Zuma Press Wire
item.media:description: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas in Mexico City in 2023.

item.title: How André Janones Helped Turbocharge Lula’s Comeback in Brazil’s Election
item.description: With street talk and tactics from the far-right’s playbook, André Janones used a WhatsApp channel to help organize millions of Brazilians online.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Ellick and Victor Moriyama
item.media:credit: Victor Moriyama for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Brazilian congressman André Janones created a digital “army” by setting up WhatsApp groups and posting on Instagram, which helped mobilized the vote for the reelection of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Lands in Miami After Fleeing Brazil
item.description: Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday’s presidential election, fled Brazil for the United States via Argentina after the police canceled his passport in relation to an investigation.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova, Edward Wong, Alice Maciel and Lucía Cholakian Herrera
item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro arriving at Miami Opa-Locka Airport on Wednesday.

item.title: The Ocean ‘Was the Color of Chocolate.’ Mexico Declares War on Seaweed.
item.description: To protect Mexico’s tourism-reliant economy, the Navy is fighting a massive sargassum bloom that dumps thousands of tons of seaweed onto Caribbean beaches daily.
item.dc:creator: David Shortell and Cristopher Rogel Blanquet

item.title: U.S. Defends Military Campaign Against Cartels as Leaders Gather in Caribbean
item.description: A regional coalition convened as part of a U.S. military effort to disrupt and combat drug traffickers that officials have compared to the campaign against the Islamic State and Al Qaeda.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt, Annie Correal and Hogla Enecia Pérez
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: A multinational military exercise near Panama City in August. Regional military leaders at a gathering on Tuesday reviewed a wide-ranging U.S. military plan to combat drug smugglers.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil for the U.S. After Election Defeat
item.description: Officials in Argentina said Mr. Bolsonaro entered the country by land then flew to Ecuador. Brazilian police had asked him to hand over his passports because of his links to an investigation.

item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro in Brasília on Sunday after hearing early results in the election he lost to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.description: Brazil’s Supreme Court told the police to seize passport of Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost the presidential election, over his links to an investigation.

item.title: Machado’s Return to Venezuela Tests Limits of U.S. Sway
item.description: Seeking new elections, María Corina Machado will need to tread carefully to avoid offending the Trump administration, while also asserting her own leadership.

item.title: How Lula’s Social Media Campaign Helped Him Win Brazil’s Election
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won another term on Sunday, with the help of a seismic social media campaign that convinced Brazilians to reject his rival.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova, Adam B. Ellick and Jack Nicas
item.media:description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s army of supporters, mobilized over a WhatsApp chat group, delivered an unexpected victory over Flávio Bolsonaro, the right-wing challenger.

item.title: Mexico’s Top Election Official Resigns Amid Corruption Scandal
item.description: Guadalupe Taddei Zavala, the head of the electoral watchdog, stepped down after facing accusations of corruption and influence peddling.
item.dc:creator: Paulina Villegas
item.media:credit: Jose Luis Torales/NurPhoto, via Getty Images
item.media:description: The president of the National Electoral Institute, Guadalupe Taddei Zavala, resigned days after the nation’s top auditing and oversight authority announced it had opened an investigation based on irregularities in contracts awarded by the electoral agency.
